I'm a 42-year-old woman, farming this 2.6 mu for 20 years since I married into this village. My husband does construction work in Shijiazhuang and my boy is in middle school, so mostly it's me and my mother-in-law managing the land. We live off my husband's wages plus whatever the land gives us, so every yuan I spend on inputs is a yuan I don't have for his school fees.

The extension agent said wheat needs 15 kg nitrogen per mu, but last year I applied 12 kg and got about 380 kg per mu, which was enough for our own flour plus a little to sell. Fertilizer prices went up again this spring, so I'll stick with 12 kg N for wheat — compound fertilizer as base at planting, then I'll topdress with urea at jointing if the wheat looks yellow. For the summer maize, I'll put down 10 kg N all at planting and that's it. I can't afford more.

For seed, I'll buy the common improved wheat variety, about 12 kg per mu. For maize I have to buy hybrid seed — you can't save it — about 2 kg per mu. Irrigation costs 25 yuan each time from the well cooperative. I'll water wheat twice: once at green-up if spring is dry, and once at heading. For maize, I'll irrigate once at the jointing stage and hope the summer rains do the rest. We usually get some rain in July and August.

I hire Old Wang's small tractor to plow after maize harvest and harrow before wheat planting — 80 yuan, can't do it by hand anymore. My mother-in-law helps with planting and weeding. My husband tries to come back for harvest. I need to keep total costs around 1,200 yuan or we'll feel it when the school asks for money.
